sentences.text: The present petition has been filed raising grievances that the petitioners have been dispossessed of the lands in question by construction of a State Highway Road from Sayla to Paliyad about 30 to 35 years ago.

The contention is that the petitioners being illiterate they did not approach the Court challenging the illegal action of the State Government in utilizing their lands without adopting due process of law.
NEUTRAL  C/SCA/16556/2023 ORDER DATED: 06/08/2024  undefin 2.1.

The averments made in paragraph '6' of the writ petition are to the effect that in the month of April/May, 2021, the officers from the office of the respondents came to the lands of the petitioners and informed that they wanted to expand the road and they would need more lands of the petitioners.
No notice however, has been served upon them.
No prior legal procedure has been adopted.

The further contention is that there is no dispute with regard to the fact that not only the State Highway from Sayla to Paliyad is passing through the lands of the petitioners, but a canal is also passing through the lands of the petitioners and reliance is placed on the map prepared by the DILR (District Inspector of Land Records Office), Surendranagar. 2.2.

As against these vague assertions, a categorical statement has been made in the affidavit of the Executive Engineer, Roads & Building Division, Surendranagar, to the effect that the petitioners were owners of the land bearing new Survey No. 50 (old Survey no. 23 paiki-1), new Survey No. 54/1 and 54/2 (old Survey No. 23, paiki,- 3, new Survey Nos. 59/1 and 59/2, (old Survey No. 23, paiki-4) and new Survey No.
55/3 (old Survey no. 23, paiki-5), situated at Village Thoriyali, Taluka - Sayla, District Surendranagar.

The statement is that to construct a State Highway from Sayla-Thoriyali, Sudamana,
NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/16556/2023 ORDER DATED: 06/08/2024 undefined proceedings under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 were initiated by the State authorities.

The village map reflecting the path way of the State Highway passing from Sayla-Thoriyali, Sudamana through the land situated in the Village Thoriyali and more particularly, the lands in question of the petitioners,
has been appended. 2.3.

It is categorically stated that a perusal of the land records, more particularly, column no. 12 therein, would reflect that the area of 9 acres and 37 gunthas of Village - Thoriyali has been acquired for construction of highway on 30.06.1964.

The notifications issued under the Government Gazette including the serial number of the relevant pages of the Government Shivrajbhai Aalkubhai vs Collector Of Surendranagar on 6 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48176260/
2 Gazette notifying the land acquisition process of the lands of Village Thoriyali and the total amount of Rs.2,693/- awarded towards the compensation is noted in the Land Acquisition Register, extract whereof is appended as Annexure-'R/2' to the said affidavit.

sentences.text: It is further stated that the details reflecting the relevant areas of the land acquired from the lands in question of the petitioners have been reflected in "Kami- Jasti-Patrak" of the records maintained by the office of the District Inspector of Land Records, Surendranagar, copy whereof is appended as Annexure-'R/3'.

It is stated that the perusal of the said documents namely, 'Kami-Jasti-Patrak' would reflect the area acquired from the old survey numbers of the lands in question of the NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/16556/2023 ORDER DATED: 06/08/2024 undefined petitioners as part of the land acquisition process.

It is, thus, submitted that only a part of the lands in question were utilized for construction of the State Highway Road and the respondent authorities have resolved to utilize the other existing portion of the acquired lands for expansion of Sayla-Thoriyali Sudamana State Highway Road.

Consequentially, the necessary work order has been issued for expansion and four laning of the State Highway has been completed as reflected in the work completion certificate dated 29.07.2022.
3.

With these submissions, it is sought to be submitted by Mr. Krutik Parikh, learned Assistant Government Pleader, that no portion of the lands in question namely, the lands belonging to the petitioners have been utilized without adopting due process of law.

4. Considering the above, having noted that the averments made in the writ petition are vague, we do not find any good ground to entertain the contentions of the petitioners that the lands in question, a part of the land holding of the petitioners had been utilized 30 to 35 years ago without adopting due process of law.
No roving inquiry as sought by the petitioners can be made within the scope of Article 226 of the Constitution of India.

It is further relevant to note that the expansion of the State Highway by four laning has NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/16556/2023 ORDER DATED:
06/08/2024 undefined also been done by the State authorities by utilizing the already acquired lands and no further acquisition has been made.
5.

However, it may be noted that for any dispute relating to measurement of the lands in question,
identification of the portion acquired by the competent authority at the time of laning of the road, it would be open for the petitioners to approach the competent authority, who shall do the needful,
strictly in accordance with law.
No mandamus as prayed for, can be issued.
The writ petition is accordingly, dismissed.
